{

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials",
      "body": "The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file does not import or declare it. This fails TypeScript checking with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if emitted without checking, every Salesforce client initialization reaches a ReferenceError after refreshing its token. Import the Prisma client used by the other adapters."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the validation result",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod safe-parse result `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials directly. This code saves the entire result as `Credential.key`. Even with credential sharing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction cannot parse that key because the token fields are nested under `data`, breaking calendar availability and event operations after a successful refresh. Persist the result's `data` property."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Define actual token fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas",
      "body": "Stringifying these Zod schema objects produces the literal property name `[object Object]`, not a wildcard for response properties. Both computed keys are the same, so the optional unknown definition also overwrites the numeric definition. Because `z.object` strips unknown fields by default, a normal synced response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates a NaN expiry, while Office365 does not advance its stored expiry. Define the supported expiration fields explicitly and preserve any required additional fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Normalize external responses for SDK-based refresh callers",
      "body": "The sync branch returns a native fetch `Response`, but the fallback can return a Google Gaxios response, a Zoho Axios response, or a HubSpot token object. Their callers still read those original shapes: Google and both Zoho adapters access `.data`, while HubSpot accesses `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. A successful external refresh therefore produces undefined data or tokens rather than usable credentials. Decode and adapt the external reply for each caller instead of substituting a raw Response for these incompatible return types."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder",
      "body": "This fallback runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits a refresh response without `refresh_token`; previously, merging that response preserved the existing refresh token. The helper now injects the literal string `refresh_token`, which overwrites the real token during the merge. The current access token works, but the next refresh sends this placeholder to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID",
      "body": "The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID and is transmitted as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, derived from `credential.id`. These IDs are unrelated. The parent service consequently looks up the wrong user or returns not found; a coincidentally matching ID can request another user's credentials. It also routes team credentials through user syncing because their credential ID is non-null. Pass `credential.userId` through to this method separately."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Authenticate outbound credential refresh requests",
      "body": "The request to the parent application's token endpoint contains only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no authentication header. These identifiers do not prove that the caller is Cal.com, yet the endpoint is expected to return third-party access tokens. The parent cannot validate this request using the configured webhook secret: requiring that secret breaks refreshes, while accepting the shown request allows token enumeration if the endpoint is publicly reachable. Send an authentication credential, such as the configured shared secret under its configured header name."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Adapt access-token-only sync replies for Webex and Lark",
      "body": "The delegated refresh contract specifies only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates the reply with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. Every reply following that contract is rejected. Lark has the same incompatibility: its new delegated call still expects the provider's nested `data` response and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need a delegated-response path that updates access token and expiry while preserving the existing provider metadata."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Delegate Salesforce refreshes to the configured source",
      "body": "Unlike the other changed integrations, this new refresh always calls Salesforce directly and never uses `refreshOAuthTokens`. Configuring `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` therefore does not make the parent application the source of truth for Salesforce credentials. In particular, synced credentials without a locally usable refresh token fail here instead of obtaining an access token from the parent. Route Salesforce refreshes through the same delegation mechanism before parsing and saving the result."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Send the actual Zoom app slug",
      "body": "The refresh request sends `appSlug: 'zoomvideo'`, but Zoom's callback stores credentials with `appId: 'zoom'`, and the credential webhook resolves app slugs against the App table. `zoomvideo` is the integration directory/route name, not the app-store slug. A parent service keyed by the same slugs used for credential synchronization cannot locate this integration, so delegated Zoom refreshes fail. Send `zoom`."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Clear invalid status when replacing credentials",
      "body": "Updating an existing credential replaces only its key. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after an invalid grant, so pushing fresh working tokens into one of those records leaves it marked invalid. The webhook returns success without restoring the integration's usable status. Clear the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 83,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make initial credential synchronization atomic",
      "body": "The existence check and creation are separate operations with no serialization or uniqueness guard. Two concurrent initial webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and create separate records. Later deliveries update only the arbitrary record returned by `findFirst`, leaving duplicate credentials with stale keys available to calendar and conferencing code. Make synchronization idempotent under concurrent delivery using a stable credential identity and an atomic or serialized update/create operation."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials
findings.body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file does not import or declare it. This fails TypeScript checking with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if emitted without checking, every Salesforce client initialization reaches a ReferenceError after refreshing its token. Import the Prisma client used by the other adapters.

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the validation result
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod safe-parse result `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials directly. This code saves the entire result as `Credential.key`. Even with credential sharing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction cannot parse that key because the token fields are nested under `data`, breaking calendar availability and event operations after a successful refresh. Persist the result's `data` property.

findings.title: Define actual token fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas
findings.body: Stringifying these Zod schema objects produces the literal property name `[object Object]`, not a wildcard for response properties. Both computed keys are the same, so the optional unknown definition also overwrites the numeric definition. Because `z.object` strips unknown fields by default, a normal synced response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates a NaN expiry, while Office365 does not advance its stored expiry. Define the supported expiration fields explicitly and preserve any required additional fields.

findings.title: Normalize external responses for SDK-based refresh callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a native fetch `Response`, but the fallback can return a Google Gaxios response, a Zoho Axios response, or a HubSpot token object. Their callers still read those original shapes: Google and both Zoho adapters access `.data`, while HubSpot accesses `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. A successful external refresh therefore produces undefined data or tokens rather than usable credentials. Decode and adapt the external reply for each caller instead of substituting a raw Response for these incompatible return types.

findings.title: Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder
findings.body: This fallback runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits a refresh response without `refresh_token`; previously, merging that response preserved the existing refresh token. The helper now injects the literal string `refresh_token`, which overwrites the real token during the merge. The current access token works, but the next refresh sends this placeholder to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

findings.title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID
findings.body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID and is transmitted as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, derived from `credential.id`. These IDs are unrelated. The parent service consequently looks up the wrong user or returns not found; a coincidentally matching ID can request another user's credentials. It also routes team credentials through user syncing because their credential ID is non-null. Pass `credential.userId` through to this method separately.

findings.title: Authenticate outbound credential refresh requests
findings.body: The request to the parent application's token endpoint contains only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no authentication header. These identifiers do not prove that the caller is Cal.com, yet the endpoint is expected to return third-party access tokens. The parent cannot validate this request using the configured webhook secret: requiring that secret breaks refreshes, while accepting the shown request allows token enumeration if the endpoint is publicly reachable. Send an authentication credential, such as the configured shared secret under its configured header name.

findings.title: Adapt access-token-only sync replies for Webex and Lark
findings.body: The delegated refresh contract specifies only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates the reply with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. Every reply following that contract is rejected. Lark has the same incompatibility: its new delegated call still expects the provider's nested `data` response and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need a delegated-response path that updates access token and expiry while preserving the existing provider metadata.

findings.title: Delegate Salesforce refreshes to the configured source
findings.body: Unlike the other changed integrations, this new refresh always calls Salesforce directly and never uses `refreshOAuthTokens`. Configuring `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` therefore does not make the parent application the source of truth for Salesforce credentials. In particular, synced credentials without a locally usable refresh token fail here instead of obtaining an access token from the parent. Route Salesforce refreshes through the same delegation mechanism before parsing and saving the result.

findings.title: Send the actual Zoom app slug
findings.body: The refresh request sends `appSlug: 'zoomvideo'`, but Zoom's callback stores credentials with `appId: 'zoom'`, and the credential webhook resolves app slugs against the App table. `zoomvideo` is the integration directory/route name, not the app-store slug. A parent service keyed by the same slugs used for credential synchronization cannot locate this integration, so delegated Zoom refreshes fail. Send `zoom`.

findings.title: Clear invalid status when replacing credentials
findings.body: Updating an existing credential replaces only its key. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after an invalid grant, so pushing fresh working tokens into one of those records leaves it marked invalid. The webhook returns success without restoring the integration's usable status. Clear the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

findings.title: Make initial credential synchronization atomic
findings.body: The existence check and creation are separate operations with no serialization or uniqueness guard. Two concurrent initial webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and create separate records. Later deliveries update only the arbitrary record returned by `findFirst`, leaving duplicate credentials with stale keys available to calendar and conferencing code. Make synchronization idempotent under concurrent delivery using a stable credential identity and an atomic or serialized update/create operation.
